text:
mira: Quick share — did a kv-layer quant bakeoff (FP8-KV vs INT8-KV) on the new 30B bring-up. TL;DR: FP8 gives ~25% memory win but we saw a nasty cold-start p99 tail with kv enabled.

alex: ugh. numbers?

mira: raw: baseline fp16 w/ kv: mem 13.6GB, p95 42ms, p99 120ms.
FP8-kv: mem 10.2GB, p95 45ms, p99 340ms.
INT8-kv: mem 11.1GB, p95 44ms, p99 150ms.
accuracy (eval suite): fp16 -> 0.0% baseline; fp8-kv -> -0.6% absolute on long-context QA; int8-kv -> -0.2%.

sam: that p99 for fp8 is huge. is it cold-start (first request after idle) or steady-state?

mira: mostly cold-start + occasional kernel fallback when kv misses cause big dequant/decompress bursts. steady-state p95 is fine. p99 spikes line up with kv-eviction + kernel switch logs.

jia: can you paste the log snippet for kernel fallback?

mira: sure:
```
[2026-03-15T21:04:12Z] request id=... kv-miss=true seq_len=2048 -> choosing kernel=gptq_dequant_fallback
[2026-03-15T21:04:12Z] kernel latency 0.246s fallback=true quant_mode=fp8-kv
[2026-03-15T21:04:12Z] memory pressure high, evicting kv pages -> blocked 180ms
```

alex: looks like dequant + eviction combinatorics. are we evicting during inference because of compacting? can we pre-warm kv pages for high-latency paths?

mira: we tried increasing kv-reserve to 1.5x for the hot path — reduced p99 by ~70ms but still worse than INT8. FP8 seems more sensitive to page fragmentation and kernel dispatch jitter.

benchbot: perf summary (microbake, 2k seq, batch=1):
- baseline fp16: throughput 120 tok/s, mem 13.6GB, p99 120ms
- fp8-kv: throughput 118 tok/s, mem 10.2GB, p99 340ms (cold-start heavy)
- int8-kv: throughput 119 tok/s, mem 11.1GB, p99 150ms

sam: how reproducible? any differences between hosted vs dedicated nodes?

mira: reproducible on ded node type-gpu-v5. Hosted (multi-tenant) added jitter but pattern same. Private on-prem with top-of-rack NVLink had slightly lower p99 for fp8 (~270ms) — likely fewer memory copies.

jia: what about hybrid options? e.g., int8 keys + fp8 values or fp8 for KV storage but int8 compute paths?

mira: we ran a hybrid: keys int8 + values fp8 -> mem 10.6GB, p95 44ms, p99 180ms, accuracy -0.25%. That seems like a promising middle ground.

alex: nice. any accuracy regressions worse than our eval threshold (0.5% abs)?

mira: fp8-kv crosses the threshold for some long-context QA slices (~0.6%). Hybrid stays inside.

opsbot: deployment note: canary rollout for quant profiles must include a KV-warmup job and kernel pin equation for FP8 to limit fallback. Recommend 10% traffic and extended canary for 48h if p99 > baseline+150ms.

sam: action items?

mira: 1) run focused microbake with enforced kernel (no fallback) to measure pure fp8 kernel latency see if fallback is primary source.
2) try hybrid-int8-keys in a dedicated canary (10%).
3) add kv-warmup prefetch for long-context routes (the qa endpoint).
4) add synthetic cold-start test in perf suite.

alex: I'll own (1) and (2). mira can you add the warmup job config and the perf test?

mira: on it — will push a small job to infra-cicd and upload results tomorrow.

benchbot: note: when you run (1) include `--quant=fp8-kv --force-kernel=fp8_fast` and capture `kv_evictions` metric.

jia: let's also capture model quality slices by context length (<=512, 512-2k, >2k) during canary. fp8 regressions seem amplified at >2k.

mira: good call — will add that to canary dashboard.

sam: ok. thanks all. this explains why some customer workloads saw regressions after we switched to aggressive fp8 profiles. hybrid seems like the safest near-term path for deployment. :thumbsup:
